title: SEA GATE
canon: Present-day Brooklyn, high summer: Sea Gate, the real private gated town at the western tip of Coney Island — water on three sides, its own armed police, one manned boom gate where the biggest city in America stops. Fraud investigator Jim Lang comes through the gate after his whistleblower client is drowned in a foot of basement water, and stays to turn the three men who stole the storm-recovery millions against each other — a contemporary RED HARVEST (Hammett, 1929, public domain) where Mary Dwight walks out clean and Lang's death is the price. NRC feature; formerly titled TSUNAMI, now canonically SEA GATE.
look: Daylight noir in July: hard vertical sun, glare off sand and clapboard, heat shimmer, a flag dead still. The look is the hundred-foot contrast — Coney Island's carnival roar (Wonder Wheel, boardwalk neon, packed beach) against the silent, storm-scarred, moneyed streets behind the fence. Nights are lit only by what is really there: ride neon, sodium lamps, guard-booth fluorescence, police light bars. Hard, dry, anti-romantic — nothing golden, nothing nostalgic.
note: Six shots drawn from the 00a synopsis (logline, drowned client, ending) and the 2026-06-14 setting bible, whose 'Tone of place' section carries the visual law — 09-visuals is an empty stub. The gate itself leads per Marco's flag: the-gate.jpg is the real W 37th St entrance (steel arch, lighthouse crest, brick guardhouse, boom) and anchors both gate shots; earlier gate generations (03-seagate-01-*, 05-investigator-gate) invented generic booths instead. Cast continuity: Jim Lang's established face is 05-investigator-gate.png (heavyset, mid-forties, rumpled grey suit) and Mary Dwight's is 03-seagate-03-mary-a.jpg — both are attached as refs where those characters appear. Warning: 05-investigator-gate.png and 08-woman-into-neon.png are letterboxed with black bars — every prompt here locks full-bleed to kill that failure. Mary's hat in the final shot follows the synopsis ('Jim's hat too big'), kept as a plain man's hat since the established contemporary Jim wears none. — 2026-07-16: six story shots appended under the Story Law (every frame must show what is happening and what is at stake). Beats mined from the 00a synopsis and the character ecosystem: Ball's porch retainer, the gate-stop beating, Connell's un-doctored survey changing hands, Mary's tally of the dead at the clam stand, the private cops letting a boss's house burn, and Jim sending Mary through the pedestrian gate as the war takes him. Jim carries the hat as an object, never worn, preserving the no-hat ruling while supplying where Mary's too-big hat comes from.

stills.prompt: The main entrance of Sea Gate, Brooklyn — the private gated town at the western tip of Coney Island — at West 37th Street, July 2026, high noon. The real gate: a grey steel arch lettered SEA GATE around a lighthouse crest, a small brick guardhouse beneath it, a striped boom across the roadway, chain-link and razor wire running off both sides toward quiet yards. A heavyset man in his mid-forties stands on foot at the boom — rumpled grey summer suit, loosened tie, shirt sweated through, tired eyes — holding his ID up to a private cop in the booth window while beach traffic idles behind him. Light: hard vertical July sun, short black shadows, white glare bouncing off the asphalt and the guardhouse brick, heat shimmer over the roadway, the haze and crowd of the Coney Island boardwalk dissolving in the deep background. Wide anamorphic composition, 35mm film still, fine natural grain, cinematic, full-bleed frame with no letterbox or borders. No text, no watermark.

stills.prompt: The basement of a condemned, storm-wrecked house inside Sea Gate, Brooklyn, July 2026, morning. A man's body lies face-down in a foot of standing brown floodwater on the concrete floor, fully dressed, one arm reaching forward. On the peeling plaster wall above him, bone dry, a child's orange life vest hangs on a single bent nail — just out of reach. Rusted pipes, a dead boiler, old high-water stains ringing the walls. Light: a single hard shaft of morning sun through a small grated window at sidewalk level, dust hanging in the beam, the floodwater throwing one slow ripple of reflection across the ceiling; everything outside the shaft falls to near black. stills.prompt: The Coney Island boardwalk, Brooklyn, July 2026, night — the last image of a film. A woman around forty walks toward camera, away from the gated town for good: a man's grey hat too big for her tipped back on her head, an overnight bag on her shoulder, the beginning of a smile she does not fully allow herself. Behind her the Wonder Wheel and the boardwalk rides burn in full red and cyan neon over a thinning midnight crowd. Light: the ride neon is the only light — a red wash on one side of her face, cool cyan on the other, string bulbs and lamp posts flaring down the worn planks; black ocean and black sky beyond the rail. stills.prompt: The deep shaded porch of a big century-old frame house inside Sea Gate, Brooklyn, July 2026, late morning. An old patriarch in his eighties — white hair, heavy cane hooked on the arm of his wicker chair, expensive open-collar shirt — pushes a signed check across a wicker table toward a heavyset man in his mid-forties in a rumpled grey summer suit, who has not touched it; spread on the table between the two men lie crime-scene photographs of a drowned man face-down in a flooded basement. Past the porch rail, a dark private Sea Gate police SUV idles at the curb, the officer inside watching the porch and not hiding it. Light: hard late-morning July sun burning the street and the hydrangeas white beyond the porch shade; under the roof everything is cool and dim, thin sun stripes cutting through the rail across the table, the check, and the photographs. stills.prompt: The back room of a small title-and-deed closing office just inside the Sea Gate fence, Brooklyn, July 2026, late afternoon, venetian blinds drawn. A woman around forty — sharp-eyed, sleeves pushed up — has just unrolled a large engineer's elevation survey across the desk, one hand pinning a curling corner, the other finger jabbing at a block of the map where it flatly disagrees with a second, cleaner official copy of the same survey lying beside it; a heavyset man in his mid-forties in a rumpled grey summer suit leans in over both maps, comparing line to line. Filing cabinets, a dead ceiling fan, a desk fan lifting the corner of the paper. Light: hard low sun slicing through the drawn blinds in flat white slats across the two maps and both faces, the rest of the room falling to shadow. stills.prompt: A weathered clam stand on the Coney Island boardwalk, Brooklyn, July 2026, dusk. At the worn counter, a woman around forty slaps a handwritten list of names flat on the boards between herself and a heavyset man in his mid-forties in a rumpled grey summer suit — five names in ballpoint, three already struck through in hard strokes — her finger pinned on the newest name, her face furious and close to his; the man looks away down the boardwalk instead of at the paper, a plate of clams untouched at his elbow. Light: only what is there — the stand's bare string bulbs and its buzzing neon sign overhead, the first ride neon coming on far down the boardwalk, the sky gone dirty orange over a darkening ocean.
